tables.name: models
tables.label: Model stack
tables.description: Every model + analysis layer in the transit4 stack: what it does, coverage, in/out summary, version, confidence tier.

tables.name: cities
tables.label: Cities covered
tables.description: Registered places the model runs, with confidence tier and role (focused vs exploratory).

tables.name: model_steps
tables.label: Model steps
tables.description: The four-step chain as editable bubble rows: inputs, generation, distribution, mode choice, assignment, outputs.

tables.name: step_links
tables.label: Data flows
tables.description: One row per arrow between steps: what data flows, which dataset feeds it, flow vs calibration loop.

tables.name: metric_families
tables.label: Metric families
tables.description: The registry of what terrain measures — one row per metric, grouped into families, with source dataset, model/layer, and honest status (live / planned / proxy).

tables.name: zone_systems
tables.label: Zone systems
tables.description: Every shape the model can run on — from raw census blocks to custom polygons — each with its fidelity to the original data and the validated conversion (crosswalk) between them.

tables.name: modes
tables.label: Modes
tables.description: Travel modes across scales — local walk/bike/bus to national rail and flights — with honest status and like-for-like comparability notes.

tables.name: wellbeing_factors
tables.label: Wellbeing factors
tables.description: The quality-of-life / happiness index registry: each factor cites the research it stands on, the data that measures it, why it is included, its cons, and a user-adjustable weight. Core factors are predetermined; everything is add/remove/re-weight as rows.

tables.name: methods
tables.label: Methods & formulas
tables.description: The modular algorithm registry: every statistical/geospatial method — what it does, when to use it, its cons, and the documentation it must carry when applied. Melting-tracts vs radius-averages both live here, documented.

tables.name: model_layers
tables.label: Algorithm layers
tables.description: The join that makes methods composable: one row per algorithm working inside a model — its role, whether it is active, selectable (calibration solvers), or planned. Add/swap/remove a layer as a row.

tables.name: run_config
tables.label: Run setup
tables.description: One row (cfg): the scenario the four-step model runs — model, tier, city, year — plus the recorded calibration snapshot fields. Tap it on the Runs screen to edit.

tables.name: runs
tables.label: Model runs
tables.description: The cockpit ledger: launches recorded in-app plus curated real run reports. Snapshot fields (model version, tier, beta, calib, zone system) are stamped from the setup at insert.

tables.name: endpoint_info
tables.label: Endpoint
tables.description: Latest /health reply from the model endpoint — replaced on every health check.

tables.name: data_inputs
tables.label: Data inputs
tables.description: Geofenced input registry: every dataset each model consumes — source, geography it covers, granularity, vintage, status, script, and what it joins with.

tables.name: model_stacks
tables.label: Model stacks
tables.description: How models separate, group, and combine: named compositions with the seams documented (what data crosses between members).

tables.name: kr_stations
tables.label: Seoul transit — model outputs
tables.description: Real output of the Korea models: every Seoul subway station (471, from OpenStreetMap) with its network-centrality scores and travel time from Seoul Station. Reproducible via tool/korea/build_korea.py.

tables.name: providers
tables.label: Providers
tables.description: Where each model actually runs — device, forge servers, hosted, or browser — as honest labels only, no endpoints or credentials here.

tables.name: routing_tiers
tables.label: Auto-router tiers
tables.description: The fleet's model-tier ladder for the Auto-router policy: which Claude tier handles which kind of task, ranked by relative cost.

tables.name: kr_district_od
tables.label: Seoul district travel-time matrix
tables.description: District-to-district (25x25) average travel time in minutes, one row per origin/destination gu pair — the district-level heatmap round-1 fallback (a full 471-station origin table would have pushed content.json over its size budget). Reproducible via tool/korea/build_district_od.py.

tables.name: kr_district_conn
tables.label: Seoul district overall connectivity
tables.description: One row per district (25): mean travel time to every OTHER district (no origin needed), plus a rank and a data-driven tercile tier (well-connected/mid/peripheral). Derived additively from the already-shipped kr_district_od table. Reproducible via a tool/korea/ build script — see DATA_SOURCES.md.

tables.name: kr_dong_conn
tables.label: Seoul neighborhood (dong) connectivity
tables.description: One row per Seoul legal-dong (424, admin_level=8 — finer than the 25-gu district layer): station-mean conn_score + a data-driven quintile tier, or an honest 'no-data' tier for the 216 dong with zero member subway stations (never interpolated from neighbors). Reproducible via tool/korea/build_seoul_dong.py + build_dong_conn.py — see DATA_SOURCES.md.

tables.name: nav_pins
tables.label: Navigate — dropped pins
tables.description: Ordered pins dropped on the Seoul glmap Navigate layer (seq/lat/lon), read by the engine's multi-pin routing to snap each pin to the nearest kr_stations node and route consecutive pins over network.geojson. Session scratch data, not seeded — starts empty, cleared via the Clear pins button.
